title: Rohit Sharma's 30 Runs in New Zealand Put World Cup Place in Doubt
excerpt: The former captain averaged 7.50 across four innings in the 3-1 series win, and Kapil Dev has left his future to the selectors ahead of the Sri Lanka series.
body:
• Rohit Sharma scored 30 runs in four innings — 0, 23, 0 and 7 — at an average of 7.50 in India's ODI series in New Zealand, even as India won the series 3-1.
  • His first-10-over strike rate has fallen from 133.68 between the 2023 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy final to 86.45 since then, according to MyKhel's analysis of his innings.
  • Former India captain Kapil Dev refused to call for Rohit's removal but left the decision squarely with the selectors: "If they take a call, his time is over."
  • His next chance to answer comes at home against Sri Lanka: Visakhapatnam on December 13, Bengaluru on December 16 and Ahmedabad on December 19, according to MyKhel.

Thirty runs in four innings, with two ducks, is not the return India planned on from Rohit Sharma in New Zealand. The 39-year-old former captain endured one of the leanest series of his ODI career as India completed their five-match tour, and the debate about his place in the side for the 2027 World Cup has moved from the margins to the centre of selection talk.

India still won the series 3-1, sealing it at Bay Oval on Sunday, November 15, when they were bowled out for 209 and defended the total by 22 runs — a game in which Rohit made 7, according to CricTracker. The team result has not shielded him, because the World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia is less than a year away and the questions are about conditions as much as form.

A series to forget

Rohit's scores in the series were 0, 23, 0 and 7, with the third ODI in Hamilton abandoned without a result, according to MyKhel. He fell for a duck off six balls in Auckland, made 23 in Wellington, was dismissed first ball by Matt Henry in the fourth ODI, and closed the tour with 7 at Bay Oval, CricTracker reported.

The fourth match was the team's low point: chasing 334, India were dismissed for 89 and lost by 244 runs, according to MyKhel. Head coach Gautam Gambhir acknowledged the worrying nature of the collapse and pointed to the similarity between New Zealand conditions and those India could face in South Africa — precisely why the senior batters' struggles carried extra weight. Virat Kohli, after 74 in the first game, followed with seven and five, MyKhel reported.

The longer record cuts both ways

The case for patience rests on what Rohit did across the two years before this dip. From the 2023 World Cup through 2025, he played 44 ODIs and scored 2,062 runs at an average of 51.55 and a strike rate of 112.67, with four centuries and 15 half-centuries, according to MyKhel, which also noted he remains India's second-highest ODI run-getter since the 2023 World Cup final.

The case against rests on 2026: 614 runs in 17 matches at an average of 39.62 and a strike rate of 101.44. The sharpest change is in the Powerplay, the phase he once owned: his first-10-over strike rate was 133.68 from the 2023 World Cup to the 2025 Champions Trophy final, with a six every 13.68 deliveries; since that final it has dropped to 86.45, with a six every 29.53 deliveries, according to MyKhel's analysis.

As recently as July he made 138 against England at Lord's, and against the West Indies in September and October he scored 32, 101 and 92. The hundreds bought him time once already: CricTracker reported that the selectors had conveyed to Rohit before the Lord's ODI in July that they were looking beyond him for the 2027 World Cup and offered him the option of announcing his retirement, and that he responded with centuries against England and the West Indies.

What the voices are saying

"If he can play, fine. I would leave it to the selectors. If they take a call, his time is over. It's entirely up to the selectors because they are thinking collectively about what's best for the game."

— Kapil Dev, former India captain, via CricTracker

Kapil Dev declined to argue either way and placed the decision with the selectors, noting that every great career ends: "Rohit has served the country admirably, and he's not going to be there throughout his life. Sunil [Gavaskar], Sachin [Tendulkar], Anil Kumble, R Ashwin, MS Dhoni — all gone, and you have to go one day," he said, according to CricTracker. Former chief selector Sandeep Patil has defended Rohit, arguing that his class is permanent and that, with nearly a year to the World Cup, there is time for a recovery, according to Sports-Now. Reports say the decision now sits with a selection committee led by Pragyan Ojha.

The alternatives are visible. Yashasvi Jaiswal, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan give India younger options at the top of the order, and every low score from Rohit strengthens their case, MyKhel noted.

What's next

Rohit's next audition is at home. India host Sri Lanka for three ODIs — Visakhapatnam on December 13, Bengaluru on December 16 and Ahmedabad on December 19 — a series MyKhel described as a likely litmus test for the opener. Runs there would not answer the harder question, whether he can score in a South African World Cup at 40, but another failure would make the selectors' decision for them.

nri_angle: Rohit's World Cup future is the selection debate diaspora fans will follow through the Sri Lanka home series in December and into the 2027 tournament in South Africa.
